q1_issues.issue: "Precursor of" is a true relational noun (the "tributary of the river" case), so *Complements of nouns and adjectives* routes its of-phrase to the ordinary genitive Possession; the nominalization-object Of oblique is reserved for a head noun naming an act, result or quality whose own underlying verb takes the of-NP as object, which "precursor" is not.

notes: The call is genuinely close - "the precursor of X" paraphrases as "what precedes X" - but "precursor" is not deverbal in English, so the relational-noun clause should govern; Of is a licensed head, just the wrong one of the two routes here. Everything else (witness for the definite singular, Member for the predicate nominal on an individual, mire_essence genus, no uniqueness atom for "the") follows the instruction set.
